# Story 01 — Admin can manage users, roles, and permissions (Story: SCRUM-34)

## Prerequisites

- Backend Prisma **User** model exists at `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` (line 52). Confirm current role/status columns before extending; **do not** rename existing columns.
- Auth module already ships `roles.decorator.ts`, `roles.guard.ts`, `user-type.decorator.ts`, and `user-type.guard.ts` under `backend/src/modules/auth/`. Reuse these; do not fork a parallel authorization pipeline.
- Settings module (`backend/src/modules/settings/`) is the closest precedent for an admin-only CRUD surface with an admin-only guard and audit-logged mutations. Mirror its module/controller/service/spec layout.
- Frontend staff area under `frontend/pages/staff/` already exposes a settings page (`frontend/pages/staff/settings/index.vue`) using Vuetify + Tailwind + i18n and the `useApi` composable. Match that stack.
- No prior story in `.squad/plans/` targets user management — this story establishes the baseline.

---

## Story Goal

Give a signed-in **admin** the ability to:

1. Create a new staff user (email, name, role, branch, department, initial password or invite flow).
2. Edit an existing user's profile fields and role assignment.
3. Deactivate (soft-disable) and reactivate a user without deleting the record so audit history is preserved.
4. Assign one of the system roles to a user; the assigned role drives the existing `RolesGuard` permission checks.

**Out of scope (do not implement here):**

- Custom, tenant-defined roles or a full RBAC matrix editor. Roles remain the fixed enum used by `RolesGuard`.
- Customer account management (that is a separate module).
- Password self-service (already handled by `auth.reset` flow).
- Bulk import / CSV.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Extend the Prisma `User` model (non-breaking)

**File:** `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` (edit the `model User` block starting at line 52).

- Add **`isActive Boolean @default(true)`** if not already present. This is the deactivation flag; do not use hard delete.
- Add **`deactivatedAt DateTime?`** to record when deactivation happened.
- Add **`deactivatedById String?`** and a self-relation `deactivatedBy User? @relation("UserDeactivations", fields: [deactivatedById], references: [id])` plus the inverse `deactivations User[] @relation("UserDeactivations")` for auditability.
- **Do not** touch `role`, `email`, `branchId`, or `departmentId` typing; only append fields.
- Add an index on `(isActive, branchId, departmentId)` to keep the admin list query cheap.

### 2 — Create the migration

**Create file:** `backend/prisma/migrations/20260910140000_add_user_admin_fields/migration.sql`.

- `ALTER TABLE "User" ADD COLUMN "isActive" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true;`
- `ALTER TABLE "User" ADD COLUMN "deactivatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3);`
- `ALTER TABLE "User" ADD COLUMN "deactivatedById" TEXT;`
- Add the FK and the composite index.
- Verify migration name ordering against the existing files listed in the tree (last is `20260910130000_add_system_settings`).

### 3 — Create the `users` module

**Create files under** `backend/src/modules/users/`:

- `users.module.ts` — imports `PrismaModule`, exports `UsersService`, wires `UsersController`. Follow `settings.module.ts` shape.
- `users.controller.ts` — routes below.
- `users.service.ts` — Prisma-backed CRUD and deactivation.
- `dto/create-user.dto.ts` — `email` (email), `name` (non-empty), `role` (enum, one of the RolesGuard values), `branchId`, `departmentId`, `password` (min length; reuse validation style from `login.dto.ts`).
- `dto/update-user.dto.ts` — `PartialType(CreateUserDto)` minus `password`; add nothing role-affecting that bypasses the guard.
- `dto/set-user-active.dto.ts` — `{ isActive: boolean }`.
- `dto/assign-role.dto.ts` — `{ role: <role enum> }`.
- `users.service.spec.ts` — mirror `settings.service.spec.ts`; cover create (hashes password), update, deactivate (sets `isActive=false`, `deactivatedAt`, `deactivatedById`), reactivate (clears deactivation fields), assignRole (rejects unknown roles), and listing (excludes password hash).

**Controller endpoints (all `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, UserTypeGuard, RolesGuard)` with `@UserType('staff')` and `@Roles('admin')`):**

- `GET /users` — paginated list with filters: `q`, `role`, `branchId`, `departmentId`, `isActive`. Return DTO **without** the password hash.
- `GET /users/:id` — single user (same shape).
- `POST /users` — create. Hash password via the auth service helper. Emit audit log entry.
- `PATCH /users/:id` — profile / role fields (do not accept `password` here).
- `POST /users/:id/deactivate` — sets `isActive=false`, `deactivatedAt=now()`, `deactivatedById=currentUser.id`. Refuse if the target is the current user (see Edge Cases).
- `POST /users/:id/reactivate` — inverse of deactivate.
- `POST /users/:id/role` — assign role; the guard already blocks non-admins, but the service must also reject setting `role='admin'` on oneself in a way that would drop own admin (see Edge Cases).

**Response shape** (list and single):

```ts
type UserResponse = {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  name: string;
  role: string; // one of the guard's role literals
  branchId: string;
  departmentId: string;
  isActive: boolean;
  deactivatedAt: string | null;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
};
```

### 4 — Register the module

**File:** `backend/src/app.module.ts` — add `UsersModule` to the `imports` array alongside the existing modules (settings, storage, auth, health, mail).

### 5 — Audit-log coverage

Confirm `AuditLogInterceptor` picks up the new controller by convention (see `backend/src/common/interceptors/audit-log.interceptor.ts`). If the interceptor is applied globally in `app.module.ts` no per-route wiring is needed; if it is per-controller, apply `@UseInterceptors(AuditLogInterceptor)` on `UsersController`.

### 6 — Refuse deactivation of the last remaining admin

In `UsersService.deactivate()` and in `assignRole()` when the target is currently `admin` and the new role is not `admin`, run a guard query: `count admins where isActive=true and id != targetId`. If the count is zero, throw `ConflictException('LAST_ACTIVE_ADMIN')`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Self-deactivation** — trigger: admin calls `POST /users/:id/deactivate` with their own id. Expected: `409 Conflict` with code `CANNOT_DEACTIVATE_SELF`. Enforced in `UsersService.deactivate()`.
- **Last active admin** — trigger: deactivating or demoting the only remaining admin. Expected: `409 Conflict` with code `LAST_ACTIVE_ADMIN`. Enforced in `UsersService.deactivate()` and `UsersService.assignRole()`.
- **Duplicate email on create** — trigger: `POST /users` with an email already in `User`. Expected: `409 Conflict` translated from Prisma unique-constraint error `P2002`. Enforced in `UsersService.create()`.
- **Invalid role literal** — trigger: unknown value in `role` field. Expected: `400 Bad Request` from DTO validation (`@IsIn([...])`). Enforced in `dto/create-user.dto.ts` / `dto/assign-role.dto.ts`.
- **Login by deactivated user** — trigger: valid password, `isActive=false`. Expected: `401 Unauthorized` with a stable code. Enforced in `auth.service.ts` sign-in path (add an `isActive` check next to the existing password check; **do not** leak the account status).
- **Existing refresh tokens for deactivated user** — trigger: user is deactivated but has active `RefreshToken` rows. Expected: revoke all `RefreshToken` rows for that user id inside the same transaction as the deactivation. Enforced in `UsersService.deactivate()`.
- **Unicode names / emails** — trigger: non-ASCII characters. Expected: stored and returned unchanged; email compared case-insensitively when checking duplicates.
- **Concurrent role change** — trigger: two admins update the same user simultaneously. Expected: last-write-wins is acceptable, but both writes must be recorded in the audit log.
- **Missing branch or department** — trigger: `branchId` or `departmentId` does not exist. Expected: `400 Bad Request` with `INVALID_BRANCH`/`INVALID_DEPARTMENT`. Enforced by an existence check in `UsersService.create()` / `update()` before Prisma throws a raw FK error.
- **Non-admin staff hitting `/users`** — trigger: staff user without admin role calls any endpoint. Expected: `403 Forbidden` from `RolesGuard`. Verify with an e2e test.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration file: `backend/prisma/migrations/20260910140000_add_user_admin_fields/migration.sql`.
- Forward: additive columns with defaults; safe on a populated table.
- Rollback: `ALTER TABLE "User" DROP COLUMN "deactivatedById"; DROP COLUMN "deactivatedAt"; DROP COLUMN "isActive";` and drop the new index. Any user rows deactivated between deploy and rollback lose their `deactivatedAt` timestamp but retain the ability to log in (since `isActive` disappears) — acceptable.
- Half-applied state: if the backend deploys before the migration runs, requests will 500 on `isActive` reads. Gate deployment on `prisma migrate deploy` completing first, as is done for the existing settings migration.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** run `pnpm install && pnpm build` in `backend/`.
2. **Prisma:** run `pnpm prisma migrate dev` in `backend/` on a fresh database; confirm the new migration applies cleanly.
3. **Backend tests:** run `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:e2e` in `backend/`. All new specs pass; existing suites remain green.
4. **Frontend runs:** run `pnpm install && pnpm dev` in `frontend/`. Log in as the seeded admin (see `backend/prisma/seed.ts`), navigate to `/staff/users`, create/edit/deactivate/reactivate a user, and reassign a role.
5. **Frontend tests:** run `pnpm test` in `frontend/`; ensure `users-page.spec.ts` and `locale-config.spec.ts` pass.
6. **Regression:** confirm `/staff/settings`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/forgot-password`, and `/auth/reset-password` still work; deactivate a test user and confirm login is refused.
7. **Lint:** run `pnpm lint` in both `backend/` and `frontend/`.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `User` model has `isActive`, `deactivatedAt`, `deactivatedById` with migration applied.
- [ ] `UsersModule` is registered in `app.module.ts` and exposes the eight endpoints listed above, all admin-gated.
- [ ] Admin can create, edit, deactivate, and reactivate users from `/staff/users`.
- [ ] Admin can assign one of the system roles to any user; the change takes effect on the user's next request (RolesGuard consults the fresh row on `JwtAuthGuard` validation, or the refresh token is rotated).
- [ ] Deactivated users cannot log in.
- [ ] Last active admin cannot be deactivated or demoted; self-deactivation is rejected.
- [ ] All mutations produce audit-log entries attributable to the acting admin.
- [ ] i18n keys exist in both `en.json` and `ar.json`.
- [ ] Backend + frontend tests (unit, e2e, component) all pass; lint clean.
